The medieval Requiem sequence Dies irae, on the Day of Judgement, opens F–E–F–D. Berlioz parodied the chant in the finale of the Symphonie fantastique and Saint-Saëns in Danse macabre; Liszt wrote variations on it in Totentanz, and Rachmaninoff and Crumb quoted it.

B♭–A–C–B♮ spells Bach in German note names. The unfinished fugue printed with The Art of Fugue introduces it as its third subject. Schumann, Liszt, Rimsky-Korsakov and Reger wrote fugues and variations on the four notes, and Webern and Pärt began a twelve-note row and a ten-note sequence with them.
